# Jubilees Chapter 15 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 15:3 — "be thou perfect" vs. "be blameless"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "walk before me, and be thou perfect" | Follows KJV Gen 17:1 |
| LOGOS | "walk before me, and be blameless" | Modern standard: "blameless" = tamim |
| PNEUMA | "Walk with me. Be blameless" | Same as LOGOS, rephrases "before me" |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. "Blameless" is the established modern rendering of Ge'ez/Hebrew tamim (Gen 17:1). EMET's "perfect" carries unwarranted connotations of sinlessness. "Walk before me" (LOGOS/EMET) is more accurate than PNEUMA's "walk with me."

---

## 15:26 — Angelic circumcision: "to circumcise all who keep the law with the angels"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "commanded the angels of the presence and the angels of sanctification to circumcise all who kept the law with the angels" | Full literal |
| LOGOS | "commanded the angels of the presence and the angels of sanctification to circumcise all who keep the law with the angels" | Same, present tense |
| PNEUMA | "commanded the angels of the presence and the angels of holiness to be circumcised, keeping the law alongside the angels" | Reinterprets: the angels themselves are circumcised |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. The Ge'ez is ambiguous but LOGOS's reading — that the command is for Israel to "keep the law" like the angels who are circumcised — is the standard scholarly interpretation. PNEUMA's "the angels themselves are circumcised" is also defensible but restructures the sentence.

---

## 15:28 — "children of destruction"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "children of destruction" | Literal Ge'ez |
| LOGOS | "children of destruction" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "children of destruction" | Same — all three agree |

**SOPHIA:** No divergence. "Children of destruction" is a Jubilees technical term for covenant-outsiders; all three preserve it.

---

## 15:31 — "spirits in authority to lead them astray"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "he has placed spirits in authority to lead them astray from him" | Full literal |
| LOGOS | "he placed spirits in authority to lead them astray from him" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "he appointed subordinate spirits to lead those nations away from him" | "Subordinate" adds hierarchical context |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. "Spirits in authority" is the Jubilees expression. PNEUMA's "subordinate spirits" is a helpful interpretation but adds something not in the source text.

---

## 15:32 — "require them at the hand of his angels"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "require them at the hand of his angels and his spirits" | Literal |
| LOGOS | "require them at the hand of his angels and spirits and all his powers" | Adds "all his powers" from fuller Ge'ez text |
| PNEUMA | "answer for them through his angels and spirits and powers" | "Answer for" paraphrases "require at the hand of" |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. "Require them at the hand of" = God will hold his agents accountable for Israel's welfare. PNEUMA's "answer for" loses the legal accountability dimension. LOGOS's addition of "all his powers" follows the full Ge'ez reading.

---

**Total disagreements: 5**
